name: Lie–Trotter splitting for linear systems
definition: For U′=(A+B)U, U(0)=U₀, with fixed square matrices A and B, define S_h=exp(hB)exp(hA), h=T/N>0, and U_(n+1)=S_h U_n for n=0,…,N−1.
variables: A,B component matrices; h step; T final time; N positive integer step count; S_h split update; U_n state
assumptions: Finite-dimensional autonomous linear system with compatible matrix dimensions, fixed finite matrix norms, fixed final time and exact component exponentials for the order argument
limitations: Generally first-order global accuracy; noncommuting components introduce splitting error; inaccurate subflow evaluations can reduce order; arbitrary matrices need not generate contractive flows
failure_conditions: Unresolved component exponential or numerical overflow
computation: Evaluate the two component exponential actions in order A then B at each step; reuse constant factors where appropriate; compare step refinements and account separately for subflow numerical error.

source.citation: Blanes, S., Casas, F. and Murua, A. (2024), Splitting methods for differential equations, Acta Numerica 33, 1–161, https://doi.org/10.1017/S0962492923000077 (publisher metadata and public formula excerpt); University of Bielefeld, Computational Physics, Operator Splitting, https://roesner.pages.ub.uni-bielefeld.de/lectures/computational-physics/semester/sose2026/lecture/08_pde/04_operator_splitting.html ; finite-dimensional error arguments independently derived.

application: General numerical integration of split linear differential systems.
required_inputs: Component operators, initial state, step and subflow policies
mechanism_note: Writing [A,B]=AB−BA, direct Taylor multiplication gives S_h−exp(h(A+B))=−h²[A,B]/2+O(h³). In any induced matrix norm both exact and split step norms are at most exp(h(||A||+||B||)); telescoping the difference of their Nth powers yields O(h) error at fixed T. If A and B commute the product is exact in exact arithmetic. Composition of separate exact flows is not an Euler update; retain as a distinct general splitting procedure.

name: Strang symmetric splitting for linear systems
definition: For U′=(A+B)U, U(0)=U₀, fixed square A,B and h=T/N>0, define S_h=exp(hA/2)exp(hB)exp(hA/2) and U_(n+1)=S_h U_n for n=0,…,N−1.
variables: A,B component matrices; h step; T final time; N positive integer step count; S_h symmetric split update; U_n state
assumptions: Finite-dimensional autonomous linear system, compatible matrix dimensions, fixed finite matrix norms, fixed final time and exact component exponentials for the order argument
limitations: Generally second-order global accuracy; error constants depend on matrices and commutators; unbounded or time-dependent operators require separate analysis; symmetry alone does not guarantee contractivity or accuracy
failure_conditions: Unresolved component exponential or numerical overflow
computation: Apply A for half a step, B for a full step and A for half a step; for constant operators adjacent A half-steps may be combined; compare step refinements and account for subflow approximation.

source.citation: Blanes, S., Casas, F. and Murua, A. (2024), Splitting methods for differential equations, Acta Numerica 33, 1–161, https://doi.org/10.1017/S0962492923000077 (publisher metadata and public formula excerpt); University of Bielefeld, Computational Physics, Operator Splitting, https://roesner.pages.ub.uni-bielefeld.de/lectures/computational-physics/semester/sose2026/lecture/08_pde/04_operator_splitting.html ; finite-dimensional error arguments independently derived.

application: General numerical integration of split linear differential systems.
required_inputs: Component operators, initial state, step and subflow policies
mechanism_note: Multiplication through degree two gives I+h(A+B)+h²(A+B)²/2, so the exact one-step defect is O(h³). The same exponential norm bound and power telescoping as Lie–Trotter give O(h²) fixed-time error. S_(−h)=S_h^(-1); with P=exp(hA/2), S_h=P[exp(hB)exp(hA)]P^(-1), so it is a conjugate of the first-order step, not identical on the same initial state. Commuting components give exact evolution. Velocity Verlet shares the symmetric composition structure for suitable separable Hamiltonian flows. Count as a splitting variant, not another distinct mechanism.

name: Matrix exponential by Padé scaling and squaring
definition: For square A, choose integer s≥0 so B=2^(−s)A satisfies b=||B||≤1/2 in a submultiplicative induced norm. Set P=I+B/2+B²/10+B³/120, Q=I−B/2+B²/10−B³/120, solve QX₀=P and set X_(j+1)=X_j² for j=0,…,s−1; return X_s≈exp(A).
variables: A input matrix; B scaled matrix; s squaring count; b induced norm of B; P,Q diagonal Padé numerator and denominator matrices; X_j intermediate approximation
assumptions: Finite real or complex square matrix, consistent induced norm, sufficiently accurate linear solve and matrix multiplications; fixed degree three is an educational specialization, not the optimized variable-degree algorithm
limitations: Overscaling can amplify roundoff and increase cost; dense matrix powers and repeated squaring may be expensive; the norm threshold only ensures denominator invertibility here and is not a universal accuracy guarantee
failure_conditions: Unresolved linear solve or loss of numerical accuracy
computation: Choose the smallest nonnegative s meeting the norm threshold, evaluate P and Q using shared powers, solve rather than form an inverse, and square s times; if a prescribed accuracy is required use a justified error policy and reject unresolved accuracy.

source.citation: Higham, N. J. (2005), The Scaling and Squaring Method for the Matrix Exponential Revisited, https://doi.org/10.1137/04061101X ; Al-Mohy and Higham (2009), A New Scaling and Squaring Algorithm for the Matrix Exponential, https://doi.org/10.1137/09074721X (public abstracts); fixed degree-three coefficients and denominator bound independently derived.

application: General numerical evaluation of a matrix exponential.
required_inputs: Finite square matrix, norm, precision and accuracy policy
incompatible_methods: Unresolved scaling, solve or precision budget
mechanism_note: Direct power series multiplication of Q exp(B) cancels P through degree six, giving local rational error O(||B||⁷). For b≤1/2, ||I−Q||≤b/2+b²/10+b³/120<1, so Q is invertible by the Neumann series. The exponential identity exp(A)=[exp(B)]^(2^s) justifies squaring. For fixed A in exact arithmetic the accumulated approximation error tends to zero as s increases (telescoping powers gives O(2^(−6s)) with an A-dependent bound); finite precision can reverse that benefit. This evaluates a full matrix function rather than composing different operators.

name: Arnoldi Krylov approximation to a matrix exponential action
definition: For square A, vector v≠0, t≥0 and 1≤m≤dim(A), set β=||v||₂ and build an orthonormal Arnoldi basis V_m starting at v/β, with H_m=V_m* A V_m. Approximate exp(tA)v by y_m(t)=β V_m exp(tH_m)e₁; return zero if v=0 and stop at exact invariant-subspace breakdown using the attained dimension.
variables: A matrix; v starting vector; t evolution time; β Euclidean norm; V_m Arnoldi basis; H_m reduced upper Hessenberg matrix; e₁ first coordinate vector; * conjugate transpose
assumptions: Finite-dimensional square real or complex matrix, accurate matrix-vector products, controlled orthogonality and reduced exponential evaluation; exact arithmetic for the stated defect identity
limitations: Dimension needed depends on spectrum, nonnormality and time; an endpoint residual alone is not a global error certificate; basis storage and orthogonalization grow with m
failure_conditions: Unresolved orthogonality loss or ambiguous breakdown
Error tolerance or resource budget not met
computation: Construct the existing Arnoldi basis, form the reduced exponential action and lift to the full space; assess error with a defect integral bound when a propagator bound is available, or a documented convergence policy without treating refinement as a rigorous certificate.

source.citation: Saad, Y. (1992), Analysis of Some Krylov Subspace Approximations to the Matrix Exponential Operator, https://doi.org/10.1137/0729014 (public abstract); Jawecki, Auzinger and Koch, Computable upper error bounds for Krylov approximations to matrix exponentials and associated phi-functions, https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.03369 (abstract); projection and defect identities independently derived from Arnoldi relation.

application: General matrix exponential action and linear evolution without forming the full exponential.
required_inputs: Matrix or linear operator action, initial vector, time, subspace dimension and accuracy policy
mechanism_note: Galerkin projection of y′=Ay yields z′=H_m z, z(0)=βe₁. The Arnoldi relation AV_m=V_mH_m+h_(m+1,m)v_(m+1)e_m* gives defect y_m′−Ay_m=−βh_(m+1,m)v_(m+1)e_m*exp(tH_m)e₁. Variation of constants bounds the error by the integral of the defect norm times ||exp((t−τ)A)||; contractivity is an additional condition, not automatic. Exact breakdown means the Krylov subspace is invariant and the lifted solution is exact. Unlike basis construction alone, this specifies a reduced matrix-function computation and full-space reconstruction.
